275	## Common Topology Patterns
276	
277	Use these as building blocks when designing your flow.
278	
279	### Linear Pipeline
280	
281	```
282	Trigger -> Action A -> Action B -> Action C -> End
283	```
284	
285	### Conditional Branch
286	
287	```
288	Trigger -> Fetch Data -> Decision
289	  |-- true -> Process -> End
290	  |-- false -> Log Skip -> End
291	```
292	
293	### Parallel Execution with Merge
294	
295	```
296	Trigger -> Prepare
297	  |-- Call API A --+
298	  |-- Call API B --+
299	                   +-- Merge -> Combine -> End
300	```
301	
302	### Loop Over Collection
303	
304	```
305	Trigger -> Fetch List -> Loop
306	  |-- [loop body] Process Item -> (loopBack)
307	  |-- success -> Summarize -> End
308	```
309	
310	### Error Handling (implicit `error` port)
311	
312	**Default: no error edge, and `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` left unset.** An unhandled node failure should fault the flow — that is the visible, correct outcome. Add error handling only where the requirements say what the failure should do.
313	
314	When they do, wire the action node's implicit `error` source port directly to a handler — this catches node-level failures (network errors, timeouts, non-2xx HTTP responses, script exceptions, transform faults). Do NOT put a Decision downstream to check for errors — by the time execution reaches the Decision, a failing node has already faulted the flow.
315	
316	```
317	Trigger -> HTTP Request
318	  |-- default -> Process -> End (success — status: "ok")
319	  |-- error   -> Log Error -> End (failure — status: "failed", descriptive output)
320	```
321	
322	**The error path must end somewhere the caller can tell apart from success.** Routing `error` into the next happy-path node, or into the same End node the success path reaches, makes every failure look like a completed run — the flow "always looks successful" while the API call it depended on never succeeded. Terminal options: a distinct End node mapping an error/status `out` variable, a `core.logic.terminate` when recovery is impossible, or a recovery branch that rejoins the happy path only after obtaining valid data (a retry that succeeded, a fallback source that returned data).
323	
324	Use a downstream Decision/Switch only for **content-based routing on a successful response** (e.g., `items.length > 0`), not as a failure detector. HTTP also supports `inputs.branches` for that. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes) — the `Error port vs other branching` table spells out when to use each.
325	
326	**Plan the error edge in Phase 1.** If the requirements mention "if the call fails", "invalid input", "article not found", or any failure fallback, add an edge from the action node's `error` port to a handler in the edge table — don't leave it to the build step. If they mention none of that, plan no error edges at all.
327	
328	### Orchestration (Mixed Resources)
329	
330	The canonical composition when more than one product is in play. Default division of labor — most "where does this step go?" questions resolve against it:
331	
332	> **RPA = hands. Maestro = conductor. Agents = brain. Humans approve.**
333	
334	- **Maestro orchestrates** — owns the case, the waits, the branching, the SLA, the long-running state (this flow).
335	- **RPA executes** — mechanical work against systems with no clean API (desktop apps, terminals, legacy web) — a `uipath.core.rpa-workflow.*` resource node. See [rpa/planning.md](plugins/rpa/planning.md).
336	- **Agents reason** — judgment calls: classify, summarize, decide which branch a fuzzy input belongs to — an agent node. See [agent/planning.md](plugins/agent/planning.md) / [inline-agent/planning.md](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md).
337	- **Humans approve** — a HITL / human-task node wraps the point where a person must look before the case continues. See [hitl/planning.md](plugins/hitl/planning.md).
338	
339	Worked example — extract, classify, and route with one human approval branch:
340	
341	```
342	Trigger -> Script (prepare) -> RPA Process (extract from legacy app) -> Agent (classify) -> Decision (confidence high)
343	  |-- true  -> Script (format) -> End (auto-approved)
344	  |-- false -> HITL (human approves or rejects) -> Decision (approved)
345	                 |-- true  -> Script (format) -> End (approved)
346	                 |-- false -> Script (log rejection) -> End (rejected)
347	```
348	
349	Here Maestro holds the case across the agent call and the human wait; RPA does the extraction the source app gives no API for; the agent makes the confidence call; the human is the gate only when the agent is unsure. Each non-Maestro piece is a separate published (or in-solution) artifact the flow references as a node — you do **not** rebuild them inside the flow.
350	
351	### Scheduled Batch Processing
352	
353	```
354	Scheduled Trigger -> HTTP (fetch batch) -> Loop
355	  |-- Queue Create (per item) -> (loopBack)
356	  |-- success -> Script (summary) -> End
357	```
358	
359	### No-API Source (RPA Feeder Bridge)
360	
361	When the source application has **no API and no connector** (legacy desktop app, terminal, mainframe screen), the flow cannot be triggered by the source directly. Bridge it: a **scheduled RPA bot scrapes the source and drops the result onto something Maestro can watch** — a Queue or a Storage Bucket — and the flow triggers off that.
362	
363	```
364	[Scheduled RPA bot]  (outside the flow — uipath-rpa + a time trigger)
365	   scrape legacy app -> push item to Queue (or file to Bucket)
366	        |
367	        v
368	Queue/Bucket item created
369	        |
370	        v
371	Maestro flow trigger -> Process item -> ... -> End
372	```
373	
374	Two ways to wire the Maestro side:
375	
376	- **Queue → flow:** the RPA bot calls `Add Queue Item`; the flow is started by a queue trigger (configured in Orchestrator — see [/uipath:uipath-platform](/uipath:uipath-platform)) or polls/consumes the queue. Best when each scraped row is a separate case.
377	- **Bucket → flow:** the RPA bot uploads a file; a scheduled flow picks it up. Best for batch drops.
378	
379	> **Tradeoff — polling latency equals the scraper schedule.** The case starts no sooner than the next RPA run. A bot scheduled every 15 minutes means up to 15 minutes of trigger latency. There is no event from a no-API source, so "real-time" is not achievable this way — tighten the RPA schedule to lower latency, at the cost of more bot runs. If the source *does* expose an event/webhook or has a connector, prefer a connector trigger ([connector-trigger/planning.md](plugins/connector-trigger/planning.md)) over this bridge.
380	
381	The scraper bot itself is an RPA project ([/uipath:uipath-rpa](/uipath:uipath-rpa)) with a time trigger ([/uipath:uipath-platform](/uipath:uipath-platform)); only the consuming flow belongs to this skill.

385	## Output Format
386	
387	Generate a `<SolutionName>.uipath.flow.arch.plan.md` file in the **solution directory** (the folder containing the `.uipx` file, not the project subfolder). The plan covers the entire solution — which may contain multiple projects in the future.
388	
389	### 1. Summary
390	
391	2-3 sentences describing what the flow does end-to-end.
392	
393	### 2. Flow Diagram (Mermaid)
394	
395	A mermaid flowchart showing all nodes, edges, and branching logic.
396	
397	**Requirements:**
398	
399	- Use `graph LR` (left-right) for all flows — Flow uses a horizontal canvas. Do NOT use `graph TD` (top-down) — it produces vertical diagrams that conflict with the horizontal node layout. Do NOT use `flowchart` — it is not supported by all mermaid renderers.
400	- Use `subgraph` blocks to group related sections — required for flows with 10+ nodes
401	- Label every edge with the port name (e.g., `-->|success|`, `-->|true|`, `-->|false|`)
402	- **Labels must be plain text only** — no special characters inside shape delimiters. The following break mermaid parsing:
403	  - `>` and `<` (interpreted as shape operators or HTML) — replace with words like "over" or "under"
404	  - `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}` (conflict with shape delimiters)
405	  - `:`, `;`, `?`, `&`, `"` (unreliable across renderers)
406	  - Use plain alphanumeric text and spaces only
407	- Do NOT put node types in diagram labels — node types belong in the Node Table only
408	- Do NOT use quotes inside shape delimiters — use `[Text]` not `["Text"]`
409	- Use only these universally supported node shapes:
410	  - Triggers: rounded rectangle `(Trigger Name)`
411	  - Actions: rectangle `[Action Name]`
412	  - Control flow: diamond `{Decision Name}` for Decision/Switch
413	  - End/Terminate: rounded rectangle `(Done)`
414	  - Connectors: rectangle `[Connector Service Operation]`
415	  - Placeholders: rectangle `[Mock Description]`
416	
417	**Example:**
418	
419	````markdown
420	```mermaid
421	graph LR
422	    trigger(Manual Trigger)
423	    fetchOrders[Fetch Orders]
424	    checkHasOrders{Any Orders}
425	    processOrder[Process Order]
426	    notifySlack[Slack Send Message]
427	    logSkip[Log Skip]
428	    logError[Log Error]
429	    doneSuccess(Done)
430	    doneSkip(Done)
431	    doneError(Done Error)
432	    trigger -->|output| fetchOrders
433	    fetchOrders -->|default| checkHasOrders
434	    fetchOrders -->|error| logError
435	    checkHasOrders -->|true| processOrder
436	    checkHasOrders -->|false| logSkip
437	    processOrder -->|success| notifySlack
438	    notifySlack -->|success| doneSuccess
439	    logSkip -->|success| doneSkip
440	    logError -->|success| doneError
441	```
442	````

445	
446	| # | Node ID | Name | Category | Node Type | Inputs | Outputs | Notes |
447	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
448	| 1 | trigger | Manual Trigger | trigger | `core.trigger.manual` | — | Trigger event | — |
449	| 2 | fetchOrders | Fetch Orders | action | `core.action.http.v2` | `method: GET`, `url: <ORDERS_API_URL>` | `output.body` (order list), `error` (on HTTP failure) | Phase 2: confirm URL and auth |
450	| 3 | checkHasOrders | Any Orders | control | `core.logic.decision` | `expression: $vars.fetchOrders.output.body.length > 0` | Routes to `true` or `false` | — |

454	
455	- **Node ID**: Short camelCase identifier used in the mermaid diagram and edge table
456	- **Inputs**: Best-guess input values based on user requirements. Use `<PLACEHOLDER>` for values Phase 2 must resolve (URLs, IDs, connection details)
457	- **Outputs**: What downstream nodes are expected to consume via `$vars.{nodeId}.*`

Every error edge you do add must reach a terminal the caller can distinguish from success — never the next happy-path node or the success End node. See [Error Handling (implicit `error` port)](#error-handling-implicit-error-port).

502	## Mermaid Validation Rules
503	
504	LLM-generated mermaid frequently contains syntax errors. After generating the diagram, **check every rule below** before presenting it to the user. Fix violations before outputting.
505	
506	### Syntax Rules
507	
508	1. **First line must be `graph LR`** (horizontal — matches the Flow canvas) — use `graph` not `flowchart` (the `flowchart` keyword is not supported by all renderers).
509	2. **Node IDs must be alphanumeric + underscores only** — no hyphens, dots, or spaces in IDs. Use `fetchData` not `fetch-data` or `fetch.data`
510	3. **Node IDs must not start with or equal a reserved word** — mermaid reserves these as keywords: `end`, `subgraph`, `graph`, `flowchart`, `direction`, `click`, `style`, `classDef`, `class`, `linkStyle`, `callback`, `default`. IDs that start with these (e.g., `endWarm`, `defaultPath`, `styleNode`) break the parser. Use alternatives like `warmEnd`, `pathDefault`, `nodeStyle` — or use a prefix like `done_warm`, `finish_warm`.
511	4. **Node labels must be plain text** — no quotes inside shape delimiters. Use `A[Fetch Data]` not `A["Fetch Data"]`.
512	5. **No special characters in labels** — these break mermaid parsing even when quoted:
513	   - `>` and `<` (interpreted as shape operators or HTML) — replace with words like "over" or "under"
514	   - `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}` (conflict with shape delimiters)
515	   - `:`, `;`, `?`, `&`, `"` (unreliable across renderers)
516	   - Use plain alphanumeric text and spaces only
517	6. **Use only universally supported shapes** — `(text)` for rounded rectangle, `[text]` for rectangle, `{text}` for diamond. Do NOT use `([text])` (stadium), `{{text}}` (hexagon), or other extended shapes — they are not supported by all renderers.
518	7. **Edge labels use `|label|` between arrow and target** — `A -->|success| B` not `A -->success B` or `A --success--> B`
519	8. **No empty labels** — `A --> B` is fine, but `A -->|| B` is invalid
520	9. **Subgraph IDs must be unique** and not collide with node IDs
521	10. **Subgraph blocks must be closed** — every `subgraph` needs a matching `end`
522	11. **No semicolons** — mermaid uses newlines, not semicolons, to separate statements
523	12. **No blank lines inside the mermaid block** — blank lines between node definitions and edges can prevent rendering in some mermaid implementations. Keep all lines contiguous.
524	
525	### Structural Rules
526	
527	1. **Every node defined must be connected** — no orphan nodes floating in the diagram
528	2. **Edge directions must match the flow** — trigger at the top, End at the bottom (for TB layouts)
529	3. **Decision nodes must show both branches** — `true` and `false` edges, each labeled
530	4. **Switch nodes must show all case edges** — one per case plus optional default
531	5. **Loop structures**: show the loop body and the loopBack edge returning to the loop node
532	6. **Parallel branches** must visually fork from one node and converge at a Merge node
533	
534	### Validation Procedure
535	
536	After generating the mermaid block:
537	
538	1. First line is `graph LR` — not `flowchart`
539	2. Check each node ID contains only `[a-zA-Z0-9_]`
540	3. Check no node ID starts with or equals a reserved word (`end`, `subgraph`, `graph`, `flowchart`, `direction`, `click`, `style`, `classDef`, `class`, `linkStyle`, `callback`, `default`)
541	4. Check no labels contain `>`, `<`, `:`, `;`, `?`, `&`, `(`, `)`, or quotes — replace with plain words
542	5. Only `(text)`, `[text]`, and `{text}` shapes are used — no `([text])`, `{{text}}`, or other extended shapes
543	6. Check each edge has valid `-->`, `-->|label|` syntax
544	7. Check all subgraphs are closed
545	8. Verify every node in the node table appears in the diagram
546	9. Verify every edge in the edge table appears in the diagram
547	10. Check for blank lines inside the mermaid block — remove any empty lines between statements
548	11. If any rule is violated, fix it before outputting

552	## Node Selection Heuristics
553	
554	Quick decision guide. For full details, read the linked plugin's `planning.md`.
555	
556	### "I need to call an external service"
557	
558	1. Is there a connector with a curated activity? Run `uip maestro flow registry list --output json` and check for typed nodes matching `uipath.connector.<key>.<operation>`. If the desired operation appears as a node type, it is a curated activity -> [connector](plugins/connector/planning.md)
559	2. Connector exists but the operation is not listed as a curated node type? -> `core.action.http.v2` connector mode — see [http](plugins/http/planning.md)
560	3. No connector exists, but has a REST API? -> `core.action.http.v2` manual mode — see [http](plugins/http/planning.md)
561	4. No API at all (desktop app, terminal)? -> [rpa](plugins/rpa/planning.md) or `core.logic.mock` if unpublished
562	
563	### "I need to branch"
564	
565	- Two paths -> [decision](plugins/decision/planning.md)
566	- Three or more paths -> [switch](plugins/switch/planning.md)
567	- Branch on HTTP response status -> [http](plugins/http/planning.md) built-in branches
568	
569	### "I need to transform data"
570	
571	- Standard map/filter/group-by -> [transform](plugins/transform/planning.md)
572	- Custom logic, string manipulation, computation -> [script](plugins/script/planning.md)
573	
574	### "I need to end the flow"
575	
576	- Normal completion -> [end](plugins/end/planning.md) (one per terminal path)
577	- Fatal error, abort everything -> [terminate](plugins/terminate/planning.md)
578	
579	### "I need to wait"
580	
581	- Fixed duration -> [delay](plugins/delay/planning.md)
582	- Wait until a specific time -> [delay](plugins/delay/planning.md)
583	- Wait for external work to complete -> [queue](plugins/queue/planning.md) (`create-and-wait`)
584	
585	### "I need human involvement"
586	
587	- Human approval or data entry -> [hitl](plugins/hitl/planning.md) or `core.logic.mock` if the app doesn't exist
588	
589	### "I need an AI agent"
590	
591	- Low-code agent tightly coupled to this flow, bundled inside the flow project -> [inline-agent](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md) (`uipath.agent.autonomous`)
592	- Coded (Python) agent, or any agent that lives as a separate project (in this solution or published to Orchestrator) -> [agent](plugins/agent/planning.md) (`uipath.core.agent.{key}`)
593	
594	### "I need an LLM to process rows of a CSV or summarize a document"
595	
596	- Add LLM-generated columns to every row of a CSV (classify, summarize, extract) -> [batch-transform](plugins/batch-transform/planning.md) (`uipath.pattern.batch-transform`)
597	- Synthesize or answer questions over one attached document, with optional citations -> [summarize](plugins/summarize/planning.md) (`uipath.pattern.deep-rag`)
598	- Small ad-hoc reshaping (map/filter/groupBy) without an LLM -> [transform](plugins/transform/planning.md)
599	- Multi-step reasoning with tool use -> [inline-agent](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md) or [agent](plugins/agent/planning.md)
600	
601	### "I need to extract structured fields from documents"
602	
603	- Source is a PDF, scanned form, photo, or email attachment with **variable layout** across inputs (invoices from many vendors, receipts, contracts, forms) -> [ixp](plugins/ixp/planning.md) (`uipath.ixp.{modelName}.{fullyQualifiedName}`)
604	- Source is already structured (CSV, JSON, database row) -> [script](plugins/script/planning.md) or [transform](plugins/transform/planning.md)
605	- Need free-form summarization, classification, or open-ended reasoning -> [agent](plugins/agent/planning.md) or [inline-agent](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md)
606	- IxP model not yet trained -> use `core.logic.mock` and surface in Open Questions
607	
608	### "The flow needs something outside flow capabilities"
609

21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<scaffolded file-format version>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:start-->
44	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
45	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:end-->
46	
47	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
48	
49	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by the project scaffold and packaging. Preserve the generated values.
50	
51	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. See [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings) below and the [connector plugin](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the connector-binding shape.

54

57	├── project.uiproj          # { "Name": "...", "ProjectType": "Flow" }

65	## Node instance
66	
67	```json
68	{
69	  "id": "rollDice",
70	  "type": "core.action.script",
71	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
72	  "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
73	  "inputs": {
74	    "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
75	  },
76	  "outputs": {
77	    "output": {
78	      "type": "object",
79	      "description": "The return value of the script",
80	      "source": "=result.response",
81	      "var": "output"
82	    },
83	    "error": {
84	      "type": "object",
85	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
86	      "source": "=Error",
87	      "var": "error"
88	    }
89	  }
90	}
91	```
92	
93	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
94	
95	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
96	
97	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
98	>
99	> ```
100	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
101	> ```
102	>
103	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
104	
105	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
106	>
107	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.
108	
109	### Instance-specific identity fields
110	
111	A few per-instance identity fields live on the node instance:
112	
113	| Field | Used by | Purpose |
114	|-------|---------|---------|
115	| `inputs.entryPointId` | All trigger nodes (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers) | Stable UUID identifying the entry point |
116	| `inputs.isDefaultEntryPoint` | Trigger nodes in subflows | Boolean marking the default entry point when a subflow has multiple triggers |
117	| `inputs.source` | `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) | For `uipath.agent.autonomous`: the inline agent's `projectId`. For resource nodes: the attached resource UUID. Definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance — no instance `model` block. |
118	| `inputs.color`, `inputs.content` | Sticky-note nodes | Visual content of the sticky note |
119	
120	Example — manual start trigger:
121	
122	```json
123	{
124	  "id": "start",
125	  "type": "core.trigger.manual",
126	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
127	  "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
128	  "inputs": {
129	    "entryPointId": "3d4a8c34-5682-4ebe-a6bc-d92a18830bb5"
130	  },
131	  "outputs": {
132	    "output": { "type": "object", "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.", "source": "null", "var": "output" }
133	  }
134	}
135	```
136	
137	### Node outputs
138	
139	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
140	
141	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
142	
143	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
144	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
145	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
146	
147	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
148	
149	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
150	
151	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
152	- `description` — human-readable description
153	- `source` — runtime binding expression, copied from the manifest `outputDefinition`. `"=Error"` for errors, always.
154	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
155	
156	**Orchestrator-job nodes (api-workflow, rpa-workflow, agent, agentic-process, function): declare `error` only — `output` is derived.** They are the one family whose instance block the converter reads: it copies an authored `source` verbatim, and injects `{output, jsonSchema, "=this"}` when a non-empty `outputs` omits `output`. So `"=result.response"` there — the connector/script source — leaves `$vars.<nodeId>.output` null at runtime while `flow validate` passes. Studio Web serializes `error`-only instances too (verified on api-workflow, published-flow, and inline-agent nodes). Subflow and published-flow (`uipath.core.flow.*`) instance blocks are never read — still declare `error` only.
157	
158	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector):
159	
160	```json
161	"outputs": {
162	  "output": {
163	    "type": "object",
164	    "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
165	    "source": "=result.response",
166	    "var": "output"
167	  },
168	  "error": {
169	    "type": "object",
170	    "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
171	    "source": "=Error",
172	    "var": "error"
173	  }
174	}
175	```
176	
177	Trigger nodes (manual, scheduled, connector triggers) have a single output — no error port. A manual trigger carries the literal string `"null"` as its `source`, matching what Studio Web writes:
178	
179	```json
180	"outputs": {
181	  "output": {
182	    "type": "object",
183	    "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.",
184	    "source": "null",
185	    "var": "output"
186	  }
187	}
188	```
189	
190	End/terminate nodes do **not** use this pattern — their `outputs` maps workflow-level output variables (see the [Author end plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md)).
191	
192	## Layout
193	
194	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
195	
196	```json
197	"layout": {
198	  "nodes": {
199	    "start": {
200	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
201	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
202	      "collapsed": false
203	    },
204	    "rollDice": {
205	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
206	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
207	      "collapsed": false
208	    },
209	    "end": {
210	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
211	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
212	      "collapsed": false
213	    }
214	  }
215	}
216	```
217	
218	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
219	
220	**What format does:**
221	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
222	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
223	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
224	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
225	
226	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).
227	
228	## Edge — both ports required
229	
230	```json
231	{
232	  "id": "edge-start-rollDice",
233	  "sourceNodeId": "start",
234	  "sourcePort": "output",
235	  "targetNodeId": "rollDice",
236	  "targetPort": "input"
237	}
238	```
239	
240	> **Gotcha**: `targetPort` is required. Omitting it produces `[error] [edges[N].targetPort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` at validate time.
241	>
242	> **Gotcha**: the source field is `sourcePort`, not `sourceHandle`. If you write `sourceHandle`, validation fails with `[error] [edges[N].sourcePort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` — the path identifies the offending edge entry exactly.
243	>
244	> **Gotcha — edge `id` MUST start with a letter (XML NCName).** Never use a bare UUID or any id with a leading digit (`"12bd09dd-…"`, `"1edge-start"`). Edge ids become BPMN `<bpmn:incoming>/<bpmn:outgoing>` IDREFs; a leading digit makes the converter silently drop those references while still emitting the `sequenceFlow`, so `flow validate` passes and upload succeeds — but the engine cannot traverse: the run reports **Completed having executed only the start node**, every output null. Use descriptive ids (`e-<source>-<target>`, e.g. `e-start-agent`); prefixing a letter (`e12bd09dd-…`) also works. Same rule applies to node ids.

306	## Implicit error port on action nodes
307	
308	Any node with `supportsErrorHandling: true` in the registry exposes an implicit `error` source port for catching node-level failures. This applies to HTTP, Script, Transform (all variants), connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes — essentially every action node.
309	
310	The port is **not** listed in the registry's `handleConfiguration`. Studio Web only exposes it when the source node has `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`; when the flow contains an outgoing edge with `sourcePort: "error"` from that node, the serializer emits a BPMN boundary error event attached to the node. Because of this gate, `uip maestro flow validate` reports an error when a node has an outgoing `sourcePort: "error"` edge but `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is not `true` — so the inconsistency is caught before publish rather than surfacing as a hidden edge in Studio Web.
311	
312	### Default: off — enable only for a failure the flow actually handles
313	
314	`inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is **opt-in, and stays off unless the requirements name a failure fallback.** Turning it on suppresses the node's fault: the node returns instead of faulting and execution continues. Enable it only when both hold:
315	
316	1. The requirements state what should happen when this node fails ("if the call fails, …", "return X for invalid input", "handle timeouts") — **and**
317	2. You wire the node's `error` port to a handler that produces an outcome distinguishable from success.
318	
319	Never set the flag on a node that has no outgoing `error` edge — it suppresses the fault with nothing to catch it, converting a real failure into a run that reports success. Let the CLI own the flag: `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set it from the error edges actually present. If you find the flag on a node with no error edge, remove it.
320	
321	### Do not swallow the failure
322	
323	An `error` edge must not rejoin the happy path. When it does, every failure walks the success route and the run reports `Completed` while the work never happened — the flow "always looks successful."
324	
325	| | Error-path target | Result |
326	| --- | --- | --- |
327	| ✗ | The next node on the happy path | Failure is invisible; downstream nodes run on missing data |
328	| ✗ | The same End node the success path reaches | Success path's output mappings run against the failed node's empty output |
329	| ✓ | A **distinct** End node mapping an error/status `out` variable | Caller can tell failure from success |
330	| ✓ | `core.logic.terminate` | Aborts the flow when recovery is impossible — see [terminate/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/terminate/impl.md) |
331	| ✓ | A recovery branch that rejoins **only after obtaining valid data** — a retry that succeeded, or a fallback source that returned data | Downstream runs on real data, not on the failed node's empty output |
332	
333	```text
334	Trigger -> HTTP Request
335	  |-- default -> Process -> End (success — status: "ok")
336	  |-- error   -> Log Error -> End (failure — status: "failed", message from $vars.httpCall.error)
337	```
338	
339	### When the error port fires
340	
341	- Network failures, DNS errors, TLS errors
342	- Request timeouts
343	- Non-2xx HTTP responses (unless caught by a configured `inputs.branches` entry)
344	- Script exceptions (`throw`, undefined reference, etc.)
345	- Transform operation failures (invalid collection, missing field)
346	- Any unhandled runtime exception inside the node
347	
348	Without a wired error edge, any of these fails the whole flow with `finalStatus: "Faulted"`. **That is the correct default, not a defect to design around** — a faulted run is visible to the operator; a swallowed failure is not. Only trade the fault for an error path when the requirements say what that path should do.
349	
350	### Wiring the error port
351	
352	```bash
353	# Confirm the node supports error handling
354	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json --output-filter "Node.SupportsErrorHandling"
355	
356	# Add an outgoing edge with sourcePort: "error"
357	uip maestro flow edge add <Project>.flow <actionNodeId> <errorHandlerId> \
358	  --source-port error --target-port input --output json
359	```
360	
361	`uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source node automatically — only for nodes that have an error edge. When editing `.flow` JSON directly, set the flag yourself **on those nodes only**:
362	
363	```json
364	{
365	  "id": "<actionNodeId>",
366	  "inputs": {
367	    "errorHandlingEnabled": true
368	  }
369	}
370	```
371	
372	Inside the error handler, `$vars.{actionNodeId}.error` resolves to the error object. For HTTP it's `{ code, message, detail, category, status }`; other nodes have similar shapes — check the node's `outputDefinition.error.schema` in the registry.
373	
374	### Error port vs other branching
375	
376	| Mechanism | When to use |
377	| --- | --- |
378	| **`error` source port** (any action node) | The node failed (exception, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch). Generic "something went wrong" handler. |
379	| **`branch-{id}` ports** (HTTP only, `inputs.branches`) | The call succeeded and you want to route on response *content* — different paths for e.g. empty vs non-empty results. |
380	| **`core.logic.decision` downstream** | Simple yes/no routing on the node's successful output. Doesn't help if the node itself fails. |
381	| **`core.logic.switch` downstream** | Multi-way routing on the node's successful output. Same — doesn't catch failures. |

487	
488	### Step 2 — Populate definitions from the registry
489	
490	Run one command per node type used in `nodes`. Copy the returned node definition object from each response into the `definitions` array, and set each matching node instance's `typeVersion` to the copied definition's exact `version`.
491	
492	```bash
493	uip maestro flow registry get core.trigger.manual --output json
494	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
495	uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.terminate --output json
496	```
497	
498	The `definitions` array must contain exactly one entry per unique `type:typeVersion` used — not one per node instance. If two nodes share the same type and version, one definition covers both.
499	
500	> **Never write definitions by hand.** The registry is the authoritative source; hand-written definitions will fail validation or cause runtime errors.
501	
502	## entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit
503	
504	`entry-points.json` declares the flow's external interface (input/output schemas and trigger entry points). Preserve its lifecycle-generated contents; project scaffolding creates it, and the Flow lifecycle regenerates it before execution or publication.
505	
506	Flow input and output parameters are declared through **variables** in the `.flow` file:
507	- **Flow inputs**: Add entries to `variables.nodes[]` whose `binding.nodeId` is the start node and whose `binding.outputId` names each input value — the start node "outputs" input values to downstream nodes
508	- **Flow outputs**: Add output variables to the end/terminate node
509	- Downstream nodes reference inputs via `$vars.start.output.<paramName>`
510	
511	The packaging/debug step derives `entry-points.json` from these variable declarations.
512	
513	## Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)
514	
515	The top-level `bindings` array (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`, `variables`, `layout`) holds resource-reference indirections for **Orchestrator resource nodes** — RPA workflows, agents, flows, agentic processes, API workflows, and HITL apps.
516	
517	Each resource node needs two binding entries (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`). The node instance itself has no binding or context data — just `inputs`. The definition (copied verbatim from the registry) carries `model.context[]` templates like `<bindings.name>` and `<bindings.folderPath>`. At BPMN emit time the runtime rewrites those placeholders to `=bindings.<id>` by matching the placeholder name against a workflow-level binding, scoped by the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`.
518	
519	```json
520	"bindings": [
521	  {
522	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID>",
523	    "name": "name",
524	    "type": "string",
525	    "resource": "process",
526	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
527	    "default": "<ResourceName>",
528	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
529	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
530	  },
531	  {
532	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID_2>",
533	    "name": "folderPath",
534	    "type": "string",
535	    "resource": "process",
536	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
537	    "default": "<FolderPath>",
538	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
539	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
540	  }
541	]
542	```
543	
544	**Rules:**
545	
546	- Add **two entries** per resource node (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`).
547	- **Share** entries across node instances that reference the same resource — do not duplicate. Matching is by `(resourceKey, name)`, so any node whose definition has the same `resourceKey` resolves to the same binding pair.
548	- Entry IDs are unique strings within the file. Descriptive IDs (e.g. `bDepositRpaName`) are preferred over short random IDs.
549	- The node instance has no `model` block — it carries only `inputs`, `outputs`, and `display`.
550	- `resourceKey` must exactly match the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` (verbatim from the registry). The runtime uses this key to scope placeholder resolution so that binding names like `name` / `folderPath` (shared across resource kinds) don't cross-alias.
551	- `resourceSubType` mirrors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceSubType`: `Process` (rpa), `Agent` (agent), `Flow` (flow), `ProcessOrchestration` (agentic-process), `Api` (api-workflow), or the app type for HITL.
552	
553	**Why this is required.** The definition's `model.context[].value` fields are placeholders of the form `<bindings.{name}>` — deliberately invalid as runtime expressions, so they can't be confused with one. Before the BPMN is emitted, the runtime rewrites each placeholder to `=bindings.<id>` by finding a workflow-level binding with `(resourceKey, name)` matching the node's manifest `model.bindings.resourceKey` + the placeholder name. Without matching entries in top-level `bindings[]`, `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder" even though `uip maestro flow validate` passes.
554	
555	**Definitions stay verbatim.** Do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the `definitions` entry — the definition is the authoring template. See "Every node type needs a `definitions` entry" in [author/CAPABILITY.md](../author/CAPABILITY.md).
556	
557	See each resource plugin's `impl.md` for the full JSON per node type: [rpa](../author/references/plugins/rpa/impl.md), [agent](../author/references/plugins/agent/impl.md), [flow](../author/references/plugins/flow/impl.md), [agentic-process](../author/references/plugins/agentic-process/impl.md), [api-workflow](../author/references/plugins/api-workflow/impl.md), [hitl](../author/references/plugins/hitl/impl.md).
558	
559	**Not to be confused with `bindings_v2.json`.** That file holds connector connection bindings for Integration Service nodes — a separate system. A flow may have both: a top-level `bindings[]` for resource references and a `bindings_v2.json` file for connector connections.
560	
561	## Bindings — connector connection binding
562	
563	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. This is configured in `content/bindings_v2.json`.
564	
565	See the relevant node guide in `nodes/` for the full `bindings_v2.json` schema, connection resource field reference, JSON examples, and the connection fetching workflow.

1 # Variables and Expressions 2 3 Complete reference for declaring variables, writing expressions, and managing data flow in `.flow` files. 4 5 > **Read this before** adding variables or writing expressions in any flow. 6 > 7 > `flow validate` catches the structural expression-reference errors: 8 > 9 > - Missing `=js:` prefix on `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` (MST-9107) 10 > - Invented `nodes..output` syntax 11 > - References to unknown variables or node IDs 12 > - Output-path walks that descend into declared primitives or schemas closed with `additionalProperties: false` 13 > 14 > Errors against **open output schemas** (HTTP response bodies, script returns, free-text agent output) and **wrong-direction reads** (e.g. reading an `out`-only variable) still slip past validate and surface only at `flow debug` or in production. 15 16 --- 17 18 ## Table of contents 19 20 - [Variables Overview](#variables-overview) 21 - [Workflow Variables (`globals`)](#workflow-variables-globals) 22 - [Node Variables (`nodes`)](#node-variables-nodes) 23 - [Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`)](#variable-updates-variableupdates) 24 - [Output Mapping on End Nodes](#output-mapping-on-end-nodes) 25 - [Expression System](#expression-system) 26 - [Available Globals](#available-globals) 27 - [Expression Contexts](#expression-contexts) 28 - [Jint Engine Constraints](#jint-engine-constraints) 29 - [Scoping Rules](#scoping-rules) 30 - [Variable Management via CLI](#variable-management-via-cli) 31 - [Complete Example](#complete-example) 32 33 --- 34 35 ## Variables Overview 36 37 Every flow has a `variables` object at the top level of the `.flow` file. It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 --- 542 543 ## Scoping Rules 544 545 ### Node Output Availability 546 547 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`. 548 549 ### Loop Scope 550 551 Inside a loop body, you have access to: 552 - All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective) 553 - `$vars..currentItem` — current array element 554 - `$vars..currentIndex` — zero-based index 555 - `$vars..collection` — the original array 556 557 Where `` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 558 559 > **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": ""` set in their JSON. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars..currentItem` will be undefined. 560 561 After loop completion, `$vars..output` contains aggregated results from all iterations. 562 563 ### Subflow Scope 564 565 Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`. 566 567 --- 568 569 ## Variable Management via CLI 570 571 There are **no CLI commands** for adding or removing variables. Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 572 573 ### Adding a workflow input variable 574 575 1. Open `.flow` 576 2. Add the variable object to `variables.globals` 577 3. Run `uip maestro flow validate` to check for errors 578 579 ### Adding node variables after manual node insertion 580 581 When adding nodes via `Edit` (not CLI), you must also add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`: 582 583 ```json 584 { 585 "id": "myScript.output", 586 "type": "object", 587 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "output" } 588 }, 589 { 590 "id": "myScript.error", 591 "type": "object", 592 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "error" } 593 } 594 ``` 595 596 > **When using `uip maestro flow node add`**, node variables are handled automatically. Only add them manually when using `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 597 598 ### Mapping outputs on End nodes 599 600 For every `out` variable, add a mapping in each End node's `outputs`: 601 602 ```json 603 "outputs": { 604 "result": { 605 "source": "=js:$vars.processData.output" 606 } 607 } 608 ``` 609 610 --- 611 612 ## Complete Example 613 614 A flow with input, state, and output variables: 615 616 ```json 617 { 618 "variables": { 619 "globals": [ 620 { 621 "id": "inputItems", 622 "direction": "in", 623 "type": "array", 624 "subType": "object", 625 "defaultValue": [], 626
