518	## IS CLI Commands
519	
520	```bash
521	# Connections
522	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json      # discover connections (--all-folders is mandatory)
523	uip is connections ping "<connection-id>" --output json      # verify connection health
524	uip is connections create "<connector-key>"                  # create new connection (interactive)
525	
526	# Enriched node metadata (pass connection for custom fields)
527	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --connection-id <connection-id> --output json
528	
529	# Resource description and metadata
530	uip is resources describe "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" \
531	  --connection-id "<id>" --operation Create --output json
532	
533	# Reference resolution
534	uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<resource>" \
535	  --connection-id "<id>" --output json
536	
537	# List all available connectors
538	uip is connectors list --output json
539	```
540	
541	Run `uip is connections --help` or `uip is resources --help` for all options.
542	
543	---
544	
545	## Bindings — top-level `.flow` `bindings[]`
546	
547	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. Bindings are authored in the flow's **top-level `bindings[]` array** (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`). At `flow debug` / `flow pack` time the CLI regenerates `content/bindings_v2.json` from these entries.
548	
549	> **Never edit `bindings_v2.json` directly.** Any manual edits are overwritten on the next debug/pack. All authoring flows through the `.flow` file's top-level `bindings[]`.
550	
551	### How connector nodes reference bindings
552	
553	The connector node's **definition** (the manifest copied from `uip maestro flow registry get` into `definitions[]`) carries a `model.context[]` template like this. **Leave the definition exactly as the registry returns it** — do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the definition, and do NOT author `model.context[]` on the instance:
554	
555	```json
556	"context": [
557	  { "name": "connectorKey", "type": "string", "value": "uipath-atlassian-jira" },
558	  { "name": "connection", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.uipath-atlassian-jira connection>" },
559	  { "name": "folderKey", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.FolderKey>" }
560	]
561	```
562	
563	At BPMN emit time, the runtime rewrites each `<bindings.{name}>` placeholder to `=bindings.{id}` by finding a top-level `bindings[]` entry whose `name` matches the placeholder. For connectors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is typically unset, so matching is **name-only** within the `resource: "Connection"` candidate set.
564	
565	> **Matching differs from resource nodes.** For `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl), the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is set to `<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>`, so placeholder matching is scoped by `(name, resourceKey)`. For connector nodes, `resourceKey` on the definition is typically unset, so matching is name-only — the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder must be unique per connector in the flow. Don't confuse the two patterns.
566	
567	### Top-level `bindings[]` shape (CLI-emitted; reference only)
568	
569	`uip maestro flow node configure` populates these entries — you do not author them by hand. The schema below is the shape the CLI emits, for **inspection** when debugging a flow's binding state and as the planned shape for the **No-Live-Tenant** flow's sidecar `<nodeId>.detail.json` (see § No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration above). Per the [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) rules, `bindings[]` is part of the CLI-owned envelope for connector / connector-trigger / managed HTTP nodes.
570	
571	For every unique connection used in the flow, `node configure` appends **two entries** to top-level `bindings[]`:
572	
573	```json
574	"bindings": [
575	  {
576	    "id": "<CONN_BINDING_ID>",
577	    "name": "<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection",
578	    "type": "string",
579	    "resource": "Connection",
580	    "resourceKey": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
581	    "default": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
582	    "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId"
583	  },
584	  {
585	    "id": "<FOLDER_BINDING_ID>",
586	    "name": "FolderKey",
587	    "type": "string",
588	    "resource": "Connection",
589	    "resourceKey": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
590	    "default": "<FOLDER_KEY>",
591	    "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey"
592	  }
593	]
594	```
595	
596	| Field | Value |
597	|-------|-------|
598	| `id` | Unique string within the file. Descriptive (e.g. `bJiraConn`) or short random (e.g. `bKEFLMRB2`). |
599	| `name` (connection binding) | The IS connection name (e.g. `"chandu.lella@uipath.com #3"`). `uip maestro flow node configure` fetches this from IS automatically — this is the supported path. The placeholder form `"<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection"` appears in the table for reference only (e.g. when inspecting a flow whose bindings have not yet been configured); it must match the definition's `model.context[].connection` placeholder (without the `<bindings.` prefix and `>` suffix). |
600	| `name` (folder binding) | Literal `"FolderKey"` — matches `<bindings.FolderKey>`. |
601	| `type` | Always `"string"`. |
602	| `resource` | Always `"Connection"` — capital C, case-sensitive. |
603	| `resourceKey` | The connection UUID from `uip is connections list`. **Same UUID on both bindings.** |
604	| `default` | Connection binding → connection UUID. Folder binding → folder key. |
605	| `propertyAttribute` | `"ConnectionId"` or `"FolderKey"` — case matters. |
606	
607	The connector node instance carries no `model` block and no binding/context data. `uip maestro flow node configure` populates only `inputs.detail` on the instance and writes the two top-level `bindings[]` entries — claiming the empty `ConnectionId` stub that `node add` hoisted (matched by name) and adding the `FolderKey` row. The connection UUID is held on the binding entry (`resourceKey`), not on the node.
608	
609	> **An empty-keyed Connection binding is a defect, not a cosmetic nit.** A `bindings[]` row with `resource: "Connection"`, `propertyAttribute: "ConnectionId"`, and `resourceKey: ""` faults Studio Web at runtime with `Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'Connection')`. `node add` hoists exactly one such stub (`name: "<connector-key> connection"`); `node configure` **claims it in place** (matching by that name), so a fully configured connector leaves no empty row — do not expect a "duplicate" empty pair, and never hand-edit `bindings[]` to remove one (it is CLI-owned). The only legitimate empty stub is the No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration case above, where the node is deliberately left unconfigured and the flow is known not to pass `flow validate` yet. An empty stub that survives a real `node configure` — or lingers after a connector node is removed — is a CLI bug to report, not something to paper over by hand.
610	
611	**Share bindings across nodes using the same connection.** If two connector nodes share the same `<CONNECTION_UUID>`, reuse the same two binding entries — do not add duplicates. Matching is by `name` only (the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder is unique per connector), so any node whose definition resolves against `<bindings.<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection>` picks up the shared binding pair.
612	
613	### Single-connector example (Jira)
614	
615	```json
616	"bindings": [
617	  {
618	    "id": "bJiraConn",
619	    "name": "uipath-atlassian-jira connection",
620	    "type": "string",
621	    "resource": "Connection",
622	    "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
623	    "default": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
624	    "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId"
625	  },
626	  {
627	    "id": "bJiraFolder",
628	    "name": "FolderKey",
629	    "type": "string",
630	    "resource": "Connection",
631	    "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
632	    "default": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
633	    "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey"
634	  }
635	]
636	```
637	
638	### Multi-connector example (Jira + Slack)
639	
640	Two unique connections → four entries in `bindings[]` (two per connection):
641	
642	```json
643	"bindings": [
644	  { "id": "bJiraConn",   "name": "uipath-atlassian-jira connection",   "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "default": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId" },
645	  { "id": "bJiraFolder", "name": "FolderKey",                          "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "default": "folder-uuid-for-jira",                "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey" },
646	  { "id": "bSlackConn",  "name": "uipath-salesforce-slack connection", "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "default": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId" },
647	  { "id": "bSlackFolder","name": "FolderKey",                          "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "default": "folder-uuid-for-slack",               "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey" }
648	]
649	```
650	
651	Both `FolderKey` entries share the same `name` but have distinct `resourceKey`s — that's how the runtime keeps them separate.
652	
653	### Generated `bindings_v2.json` (reference only — do not edit)
654	
655	At debug/pack time, the CLI derives `content/bindings_v2.json` from the top-level `bindings[]` above. One `Connection` resource per unique `resourceKey`; the `FolderKey` bindings are absorbed as metadata (they do not produce standalone resource entries). The generated output looks like:
656	
657	```json
658	{
659	  "version": "2.0",
660	  "resources": [
661	    {
662	      "resource": "Connection",
663	      "key": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
664	      "id": "Connection7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
665	      "value": {
666	        "ConnectionId": {
667	          "defaultValue": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
668	          "isExpression": false,
669	          "displayName": "my-jira-connection"
670	        }
671	      },
672	      "metadata": {
673	        "ActivityName": "Create Issue",
674	        "BindingsVersion": "2.2",
675	        "DisplayLabel": "my-jira-connection",
676	        "UseConnectionService": "true",
677	        "Connector": "uipath-atlassian-jira"
678	      }
679	    }
680	  ]
681	}
682	```
683	
684	- `id` is always `"Connection" + <resourceKey>` (concatenated, no separator) — generated, not authored.
685	- `metadata.Connector` is derived from the definition's `model.context[].connectorKey`.
686	- `metadata.ActivityName` comes from the matched node's `display.label`.
687	
688	### Other binding resource types (triggers, queues, scheduled)
689	
690	For connector-trigger flows, the same pattern applies — top-level `bindings[]` entries with additional metadata; the CLI derives `EventTrigger` and `Property` resources for `bindings_v2.json`. See [connector-trigger/impl.md](../connector-trigger/impl.md) for the trigger-specific shape.
691	
692	| Generated `bindings_v2.json` resource | Authored via | Key source fields |
693	|---------------------------------------|--------------|-------------------|
694	| `Connection` | Top-level `bindings[]` with `resource: "Connection"`, `propertyAttribute: "ConnectionId"` | Covered above |
695	| `EventTrigger` | Top-level `bindings[]` + the trigger node itself | See connector-trigger plugin |
696	| `Property` | Trigger node's `model.inputs.filterFields` | See connector-trigger plugin |
697	| `Queue` / `TimeTrigger` | Specific trigger types | See relevant trigger plugin |
698	
699	> **Never hardcode connection IDs.** Always fetch them from IS at authoring time. Connection IDs are tenant-specific and change across environments.
700	
701	---
702	
703	## Debug
704	
705	### Common Errors
706	
707	| Error | Cause | Fix |
708	| --- | --- | --- |
709	| No connection found | Connection not bound — top-level `bindings[]` missing or `resourceKey` doesn't match the node | Run Step 1 above to bind a connection; verify both entries (`ConnectionId` + `FolderKey`) are in the top-level `bindings[]` |
710	| Connection ping failed | Connection expired or misconfigured | Re-authenticate the connection in the IS portal |
711	| Missing `inputs.detail` | Node added but not configured | Run `uip maestro flow node configure` with the detail JSON (Step 6) |
712	| Reference field has display name instead of ID | `uip is resources run list` was skipped | Resolve the reference field to get the actual ID (Step 4) |
713	| Node faults at runtime with "resource not found" or similar after a clean build and validate | Reference field uses an ID scoped to a **different** connection (common when copying from a prior flow in the same session — e.g., a Slack channel ID from workspace A pasted into a node bound to workspace B's connection) | Re-run `uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" --connection-id <CURRENT_CONNECTION_ID>`, extract the fresh ID, update `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` in `--detail`, re-run `node configure`, re-debug. See Step 4 and the top-level Anti-Pattern on reference-ID reuse in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md). |
714	| Required field missing at runtime | Required input field not provided | Check metadataFile for all `required: true` fields in both `requestFields` and `parameters` |
715	| `$vars` expression unresolvable | Node outputs block missing or node not connected | Verify the node has edges and upstream outputs are correctly referenced |
716	| `connectorMethodInfo` missing method/path | Used `registry get` without `--connection-id` | Re-run with `--connection-id` for enriched metadata (Step 2) |
717	| `bindings_v2.json` malformed or stale | It was hand-edited (the CLI overwrites edits on next debug/pack), or top-level `bindings[]` was mutated by hand | Never edit `bindings_v2.json` directly. Re-run `uip maestro flow node configure` on the affected connector node(s) so the CLI re-emits top-level `bindings[]`; `bindings_v2.json` is regenerated from those at the next debug/pack. Compare the emitted shape against the CLI-emitted reference in § Top-level `bindings[]` shape. |
718	| Connector key not found | Wrong key name | Run `uip is connectors list --output json` — keys are often prefixed with `uipath-` |
719	| FilterBuilder UI shows `undefined` when activity is reopened in Studio Web; flow runs at debug | A raw `queryParameters.<filterParamName>` string was passed instead of a structured filter tree, so `essentialConfiguration.savedFilterTrees.<filterParamName>` is empty. The runtime side works but Studio Web has no tree to render. | Re-run `uip maestro flow node configure` with `--detail '{"filter": {...tree...}}'` — the CLI populates both halves. See Step 6a above and [uipath-platform — Filter Trees (CEQL)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/activities.md#filter-trees-ceql). |
720	| `node configure` fails with `'<name>' is a FilterBuilder parameter — pass a structured filter tree under --detail.filter` | Same root cause — raw string under `queryParameters` for a FilterBuilder param | Move the value into `--detail.filter` as a structured tree. The CLI catches this at configure time so it never reaches Studio Web. |
721	| Data Service query returns every record (or faults with malformed CEQL ending in `AND`) though a filter tree was configured; `node configure` reported Success | A filter-tree leaf's field id did not match the entity schema (matching is case-sensitive). The compiler drops unmatched leaves without an error — one bad leaf empties the query string, a bad leaf beside a good one leaves a dangling `AND`. | Compare the tree's field ids against the entity schema — `uip df entities list --output json` for the entity `Id`, then `uip df entities get <entity-id> --output json` for the field names. Re-run `node configure` with the exact ids. See Step 6a. |
722	| Node faults `[102003] Integration Services bad request`, IS 400 `"Expected a field name expression but got 'StringValue'"` — `flow validate` passed | Hand-authored CEQL string (e.g. Data Service `queryExpression`) quotes the **field name**: `'accountNumber' = '...'`. CEQL reads a quoted token as a string literal. Only `node configure --detail.filter` builds the expression for you; a string hand-written into the `.flow` JSON reaches IS unchecked. | Field names bare, only values quoted: `` `accountNumber = '${$vars...}'` ``. Or author via `--detail.filter` so the CLI compiles the CEQL. |
723	| Node faults `[102003] Integration Services bad request`, IS 400 `"Unsupported value expression 'Column' on field '<field>'"` — `flow validate` passed | Hand-authored CEQL double-quotes the **value**, typically from a concatenation with escaped quotes: `` =js:"accountNumber = \"" + String(v) + "\"" ``. CEQL reads a double-quoted token as a column reference, not a string literal. | Single-quote the value inside the concatenation: `` =js:"accountNumber = '" + String($vars.<node>.output.<field>) + "'" ``. Or author via `--detail.filter`. See [Hand-authored CEQL strings](#hand-authored-ceql-strings). |
724	| Node faults `[102003] Integration Services bad request` and the filter uses `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `ge`, `lt`, or `le` | OData aliases in a hand-authored CEQL string. CEQL accepts only symbol operators. | Replace with `=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`. See the alias table in [Hand-authored CEQL strings](#hand-authored-ceql-strings). |
725	| `node configure` fails with `customFieldsRequestDetails.parameterValues must be an array of [key, value] tuples, not an object map` | Wrote `parameterValues: {key: value}` (object map). Studio Web emits its `Map<string,string\|null>` as `Array.from(entries())` — tuples, not object | Convert to tuples: `[["key", "value"], ...]`. See Step 6c. |
726	| Custom fields fault at runtime with token unresolved | A `{token}` in `objectActions[].apiConfiguration.url` or `body` has no entry in `parameterValues` | Re-read the ObjectAction's `apiConfiguration` placeholders, add the missing tuple to `parameterValues`. CLI does not validate token coverage. |
727	| `node configure` fails with `customFieldsRequestDetails has unknown keys: ObjectActionName, ParameterValues` | PascalCase inner keys instead of camelCase | Use `objectActionName` / `parameterValues`. Studio Web emits camelCase; PascalCase is rejected. |
728	| Field rejected at runtime as unknown (e.g. `"unknown field 'fields.labels[*]'"`) after a clean `flow validate` | `[*]` was left in the `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` key. `[*]` is an array marker from `requestFields[].name`, not part of the wire key. | Strip `[*]` from the key in your `--detail` payload, pass a `=js:` expression returning the array, and re-run `node configure`. Fields with `[*].` (segments after the `[*]`) are not authorable. See the array-fields table in Step 6b. |
729	| Array field round-trips empty after a clean `flow validate` | Literal JSON array authored for a `[*]` field — validates but does not bind | Author as `=js:` expression returning the array: `"users": "=js:(['U123ABC', 'U456DEF'])"`. See the array-fields table in Step 6b. |
730	
731	### Debug Tips
732	
733	1. **Always check top-level `bindings[]` in the `.flow` file** — connector nodes silently fail if a binding is missing or malformed. Compare against the CLI-emitted `bindings[]` shape documented above (§ Top-level `bindings[]` shape). Do not inspect `bindings_v2.json` as ground truth; it is regenerated from the `.flow` on every debug/pack.
734	2. **Compare inputs against metadataFile** — the full metadata (from `is resources describe`) has every field with types, descriptions, and whether it's required
735	3. **`flow validate` does NOT catch connector-specific issues** — validation only checks JSON schema and graph structure. Missing `inputs.detail` fields, wrong reference IDs, and expired connections are caught only at runtime (`flow debug`)
736	4. **If a connector key doesn't work** — list all connectors: `uip is connectors list --output json`. Keys are often prefixed with `uipath-`
737	5. **Query/path parameters** — some required parameters appear only in the metadataFile `parameters` section, not in `requestFields`. Check both.
738	6. **`node configure` populates bindings automatically** — it appends the two top-level `bindings[]` entries and populates `inputs.detail`. The generated `bindings_v2.json` follows from these at debug/pack time. If you cannot run `node configure` (no live tenant, sandbox forbids it, planning-only request), record the planned binding entries in the sidecar `<nodeId>.detail.json` per the No-Live-Tenant flow above — do not author `bindings[]` directly on the `.flow` as a substitute, and note that the flow will not pass `flow validate` until a real `node configure` runs.
739

commands.result_summary:
65:## Filter Trees (CEQL)
66-
67-Some IS activities — most notably **List All Records** and other list/query operations — accept a server-side filter expressed in **CEQL** (Connector Expression Query Language). As with trigger filters (which compile to JMESPath), CEQL filters are authored as a **structured filter tree** and the CLI compiles them to a CEQL string. Authoring as a tree keeps the CLI and Studio Web in lockstep so the activity round-trips cleanly when re-opened in SW.
68-
69-### Contract — three signals from IS metadata
70-
71-The CLI reads the live IS metadata response and uses three signals to wire the filter:
72-
73-1. **The activity supports CEQL** when one of its `parameters` declares `design.component === "FilterBuilder"`. That parameter's `name` is the connector-specific key the compiled CEQL string is sent under — most commonly `where`, but **not always** (e.g. Salesforce uses `q`). Activities with no such parameter do not support server-side filtering — pass no `filter` and filter downstream.
74-2. **A field is filterable** when its IS metadata entry has `searchable: true`. Type alone does not gate it — the connector flags fields explicitly. Fields without `searchable: true` are rejected by the CLI even if they look like primitives.
75-3. **Permitted operators** for the field are listed under `searchableOperators`. **Connector-side identifier** for the field in CEQL is `searchableNames[0]` when present (some connectors expose a friendly `name` but require a different identifier in the query string).
76-
77-### What the CLI persists from a single `filter` input
78-
79-- **Runtime side** — the compiled CEQL string lands at `inputs.detail.queryParameters.<filterParamName>` where `<filterParamName>` is the FilterBuilder parameter's name from the IS metadata (often `where`).
80-- **Design-time side** — the structured tree is embedded under `inputs.detail.configuration`'s `essentialConfiguration.savedFilterTrees.<filterParamName>`. Studio Web reads this on open to re-render the filter widget; without it the filter UI shows up empty even though the runtime call still works.
81-
82-Pass `filter` (the structured tree) and the CLI emits both halves in lockstep. Passing both `filter` and `queryParameters.<filterParamName>` is rejected at validation time — single source of truth.
83-
84-### Tree shape
85-
86-Identical to the trigger filter tree — the same `FilterTree` / `Filter` / `WorkflowValue` types are used; only the compiler output (CEQL vs JMESPath) differs.
87-
88-```jsonc
89-{
90-  "groupOperator": 0,             // 0 = And, 1 = Or — combines sibling filters/groups
91-  "index": 0,                     // ordering index within parent (root is 0)
92-  "filters": [                    // leaf conditions at this level
93-    {
94-      "id": "<fieldName>",        // resource field name from `is resources describe`
95-      "operator": "<Operator>",   // PascalCase, see operator table below
96-      "value": {
97-        "value": <typed value>,   // string / number / boolean / ISO-8601 date-time / array
98-        "rawString": "\"...\"",   // verbatim user-entered text (with quotes for strings)
99-        "isLiteral": true         // literals only — expression values are not yet supported
100-      }
101-    }
102-  ],
103-  "groups": []                    // optional: nested subgroups (same shape as root)
104-}
105-```
106-
107-A no-op filter — used when the user wants to list all records without restriction — is `null` or `{"groupOperator": null, "index": 0, "filters": []}`. Prefer **omitting** the `filter` field entirely.
108-
109-### Compiled CEQL output
110-
111-The CLI compiles each leaf to `<field> <op> <value>` (or `<field> <function>` for null checks) and joins siblings with the group operator. String values are wrapped in single quotes; booleans, numerics, and enums are passed bare.
112-
113-| Operator | CEQL token | Notes |
114-|---|---|---|
115-| `Equals` | `=` | |
116-| `NotEquals` | `!=` | |
117-| `LessThan` / `LessThanOrEqual` / `GreaterThan` / `GreaterThanOrEqual` | `<` / `<=` / `>` / `>=` | Numeric / date-time |
118-| `Contains` / `NotContains` | `Contains` / `Not Contains` | Substring (string) |
119-| `StartsWith` / `NotStartsWith` / `EndsWith` / `NotEndsWith` | `Starts With` / `Not Starts With` / `Ends With` / `Not Ends With` | String |
120-| `Like` / `NotLike` | `Like` / `Not Like` | Pattern match (connector-specific) |
121-| `In` / `NotIn` | `In` / `Not In` | Membership — `value.value` is a list; rendered as `(v1, v2, …)` |
122-| `IsNull` / `IsNotNull` | `Is Null` / `Is Not Null` | No `value` needed |
123-| `Is` / `IsNot` | `=` against literal `true` / `false` | Boolean shortcut |
124-
125-Logical operators between siblings:
126-
127-| `groupOperator` | CEQL token |
128-|---|---|
129-| `0` (And) | ` AND ` |
130-| `1` (Or) | ` OR ` |
131-
132-### Examples
133-
134-**Active accounts only:**
135-
136-```json
137-{
138-  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
139-  "filters": [
140-    { "id": "Status", "operator": "Equals",
141-      "value": { "value": "Active", "rawString": "\"Active\"", "isLiteral": true } }
142-  ]
143-}
144-```
145-→ CEQL: `Status = 'Active'`
146-
147-**Score ≥ 80 AND Region in (EMEA, APAC):**
148-
149-```json
150-{
151-  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
152-  "filters": [
153-    { "id": "Score", "operator": "GreaterThanOrEqual",
154-      "value": { "value": 80, "rawString": "80", "isLiteral": true } },
155-    { "id": "Region", "operator": "In",
156-      "value": { "value": ["EMEA", "APAC"], "rawString": "[\"EMEA\",\"APAC\"]", "isLiteral": true } }
157-  ]
158-}
159-```
160-→ CEQL: `Score >= 80 AND Region In ('EMEA', 'APAC')`
161-
162-**Subject contains "urgent" AND (owner = me OR owner is null):**
163-
164-```json
165-{
166-  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
167-  "filters": [
168-    { "id": "Subject", "operator": "Contains",
169-      "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true } }
170-  ],
171-  "groups": [
172-    {
173-      "groupOperator": 1, "index": 1,
174-      "filters": [
175-        { "id": "OwnerId", "operator": "Equals",
176-          "value": { "value": "${me.id}", "rawString": "\"${me.id}\"", "isLiteral": false } },
177-        { "id": "OwnerId", "operator": "IsNull" }
178-      ]
179-    }
180-  ]
181-}
182-```
183-→ CEQL: `Subject Contains 'urgent' AND (OwnerId = ${me.id} OR OwnerId Is Null)`. Non-literal values (`isLiteral: false`) are emitted as `${expression}` placeholders for runtime resolution.
184-
185-### How to build a CEQL filter tree
186-
187-1. Run `uip is resources describe "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" --connection-id "<id>" --operation List` to read the resource's metadata.
188-2. **Confirm CEQL is supported** for this operation: at least one entry under `parameters` must carry `design.component === "FilterBuilder"`. If none does, the activity does not support server-side filtering — omit `filter` and filter downstream (e.g. with a Script node).
189-3. **Pick filterable fields** from `fields[]` where `searchable: true`. Other fields will be rejected by the CLI at configure time even if they look like primitives.
190-4. For each leaf, pick an operator from the field's `searchableOperators` list (when present). Date-time fields take ISO-8601 strings; enums take the literal enum value.
191-5. Use the field's `name` as the leaf `id`. The CLI rewrites it to `searchableNames[0]` when emitting CEQL if the connector declares one — you don't need to use the alias yourself.
192-6. Build one leaf per condition; place multiple conditions under the same `groupOperator` (0 for AND, 1 for OR). Use nested `groups` for mixed AND/OR.
193-7. Wrap values in a `WorkflowValue` object with `value`, `rawString`, `isLiteral`. Strings, numbers, booleans, dates, and arrays are all valid `value` types; only `isLiteral: true` is currently supported by activity-side compilation.
194-
195-### What NOT to generate
196-
197-| Invalid input | Why it fails | Valid replacement |
198-|---|---|---|
199-| `"filter": "Status = 'Active'"` | Bare CEQL string — `filter` must be an object. | Structured tree with `filters: [...]`. |
200-| `"filterExpression": "..."` | That field is reserved for the trigger (JMESPath) path. | Use `filter` (CEQL tree) for activities. |
201-| `{ "operator": "equals", ... }` | Operator is case-sensitive. | `"operator": "Equals"` |
202-| `{ "value": "Active" }` on a leaf | Bare string — must be wrapped in the `WorkflowValue` object. | `{ "value": { "value": "Active", "rawString": "\"Active\"", "isLiteral": true } }` |
203-| `{ "id": "fields.Status", ... }` | `fields.` prefix — use the bare field name from `is resources describe`. | `{ "id": "Status", ... }` |
204-| `{ "id": "<field without searchable: true>", ... }` | The CLI checks `searchable` on the IS metadata entry; non-searchable fields are rejected even if their type looks filterable. | Pick a field where `searchable: true`. |
205-| `"queryParameters": { "where": "..." }` alongside `filter` | Hardcoding `where` assumes that's the FilterBuilder param name — it isn't always (Salesforce uses `q`, etc.). | Pass `filter` only; the CLI discovers the right param name from `design.component === "FilterBuilder"`. |
206-| `In` operator with a single value not in a list | `In` expects an array `value`. | Use `Equals`, or pass `value: ["one"]`. |
207-
208-## Custom Fields (`objectActions[ActionType=Api]`)
209-
210-Connectors with extensible/custom fields (Jira project+issuetype → custom Jira fields, Mailchimp list_id → audience merge fields, Salesforce custom objects) expose `Api`-type entries under `objectActions[]`. Each entry's `apiConfiguration.url`/`body` carries `{token}` placeholders naming the parent fields. The runtime replays the ObjectAction with cached parent values to fetch the connector-specific custom-field schema.
211-
212-**For Maestro flows**, this lives on the activity node as `essentialConfiguration.customFieldsRequestDetails`. Authoring contract → [uipath-maestro-flow connector/impl.md Step 6c](../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md).

12:- Parent-Field-Driven Custom Fields (api-type ObjectActions)
13-- Execute Operations
14-- Pagination
15-- Execute Error Handling
16-
17-For reference field resolution (simple refs, dependency chains, required field validation), see [reference-resolution.md](reference-resolution.md).
18-
19----
20-
21-## Listing and Describing Resources
22-
23-**Always pass `--connection-id`** to get connection-specific metadata including custom objects and fields. Without it, only standard objects/fields are returned.
24-
25-## Response Fields
26-
27-| Field | Description |
28-|---|---|
29-| **`Name`** | Resource identifier (used in commands) |
30-| `DisplayName` | Human-readable name |
31-| `Path` | API path for this resource |
32-| `Type` | Resource type (standard, custom) |
33-| `SubType` | Sub-type (e.g., method, entity) |
34-
35-## Describe Response
36-
37-The describe command returns metadata from the raw API. The output depends on whether `--operation` is provided.
38-
39-### Without `--operation` — operation summary
40-
41-Returns which operations the resource supports:
42-
43-| Field | Description |
44-|---|---|
45-| **`availableOperations`** | List of operations — each with `method` (GET/POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE), `name` (Create/List/etc.), `description`, `curated` (display name) |
46-| **`hint`** | Instructs to use `--operation` for field details |
47-
48-### With `--operation` — per-operation field detail
49-
50-Returns the full field breakdown for the specified operation:
51-
52-| Field | Description |
53-|---|---|
54-| **`operation`** | Operation info — `method`, `name`, `description`, `path`, `curated` display name |
55-| **`parameters`** | Path and query parameters (NOT body fields) — each with `name`, `type` (path/query), `dataType`, `required`, `defaultValue`, `reference` |
56-| **`requestFields`** | Fields to send in `--body` — each with `name`, `type`, `displayName`, `required`, `description`, `reference`, `enum` |
57-| **`responseFields`** | Fields returned in the response — each with `name`, `type`, `displayName` |
58-
59-> **Always use `--operation`** to get actionable field detail. Without it you only see which operations exist.
60-
61-### Key field properties
62-
63-- **`required: true`** — field must be provided in `--body` or `--query`. Do NOT skip.
64-- **`reference`** — field value must be looked up from another resource. See [reference-resolution.md](reference-resolution.md). When baking a static value for a reference field, also emit `designTimeMetadata.designTimeLookups` so the edit-UI renders a label — see [reference-resolution.md — Static Reference-Value Labeling](reference-resolution.md#static-reference-value-labeling).
65-- **`enum`** — field only accepts the listed values (e.g., `["low", "normal", "high"]`).
66-
67-Results are cached locally. Use `--refresh` to bypass cache after re-auth or schema changes.
68-
69----
70-
71-## Describe Failures
72-
73-Some resources return an error on describe. This is a **server-side metadata gap** — do not retry with `--refresh`.
74-
75-**Recovery:**
76-
77-1. **Skip describe entirely** — do not waste calls retrying.
78-2. **Infer fields from user context** — use the field names and values the user provided in their request.
79-3. **Infer reference fields from naming** — see [reference-resolution.md — Inferring References Without Describe](reference-resolution.md#inferring-references-without-describe).
80-4. **Attempt execute directly** — let the server validate. If a field is rejected, read the error and adjust.
81-
82----
83-
84:## Parent-Field-Driven Custom Fields (api-type ObjectActions)
85-
86-For connectors whose required fields depend on parent-field selections (Jira `GenerateSchema` keyed off project + issue type, Salesforce SOQL `GenerateQuerySchema` keyed off the query string, Dataservice V3 `FetchObjectMetadataTenant` keyed off `tenantEntityName`), the base `describe` returns only base fields. To preview the full required-field set the runtime will see, pass parent values via `-f, --field`:
87-
88-```bash
89-# Jira: project + issue type → custom fields (GET, query-param tokens)
90-uip is resources describe uipath-atlassian-jira curated_create_issue \
91-  --connection-id "<id>" --operation Create \
92-  -f fields.project.key=ENGCE \
93-  -f fields.issuetype.id=3 \
94-  --output json
95-
96-# Salesforce SOQL: query string → response columns (POST, body token)
97-uip is resources describe uipath-salesforce-sfdc query_records \
98-  --connection-id "<id>" --operation Create \
99-  -f query="SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE Status = 'Active'" \
100-  --output json
101-```
102-
103-What it does — runs the matching api-type ObjectAction against the IS Element Service (same path Studio Web's dispatcher uses), then merges the response into `requestFields` per the action's `onSuccess.remapConfiguration`. Use it before validating required fields to catch project- or operation-specific mandatory fields the base describe can't see.
104-
105-| Flag | Notes |
106-|------|-------|
107-| `-f, --field <name=value>` | Repeatable. Token names match `apiConfiguration.url` and `apiConfiguration.body` placeholders verbatim — no `_sub_` encoding (encoding only applies when caching parent values for runtime replay; see [activities.md — Custom Fields](activities.md#custom-fields-objectactionsactiontypeapi)). |
108-| `--action <name>` | Optional. Disambiguates when more than one api-type action could match the field set. |
109-
110-Requires `--connection-id` and `--operation`. Cache is bypassed when `--field` is supplied — the action response varies per parent-field combination. The merge mode (`replace` / `append` / `prepend` / `noop`) comes from the action's `remapConfiguration.input`; for Jira `GenerateSchema` it is `replace`.
111-
112-When no api-type action's `rules[]` are satisfied by the supplied fields, the CLI errors with `No api-type ObjectAction matched for fields [...]`. List the operation's actions from the describe output's `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` (or top-level `objectActions[]` for older shapes) to see which fields each action requires.
113-
114----
115-
116-## Execute Operations
117-
118-| Verb | Description | `--body` | `--query` |
119-|---|---|---|---|
120-| `create` | Create a new record | Yes | No |
121-| `list` | Retrieve multiple records | No | Optional (`limit=10&offset=0`) |
122-| `get` | Get a single record by ID | No | Yes (`id=<RECORD_ID>`) |
123-| `update` | Partial update (PATCH) | Yes | Yes (`id=<RECORD_ID>`) |
124-| `delete` | Delete a record | No | Yes (`id=<RECORD_ID>`) |
125-| `replace` | Full replacement (PUT) | Yes | Yes (`id=<RECORD_ID>`) |
126-
127-> **Update** (PATCH) = change specific fields. **Replace** (PUT) = overwrite entire record. Default to **Update** unless the user says "replace" or "overwrite".
128-
129-### Filtering Results with `--output-filter`
130-
131-Use the global `--output-filter` flag with a JMESPath expression to extract specific fields from large responses if possible via JMESPath.
132-
133-```bash
134-# Extract only id, name, and email from a user list
135-uip is resources run list "<CONNECTOR_KEY>" "<OBJECT_NAME>" \
136-  --connection-id "<CONNECTION_ID>" \
137-  --output json \
138-  --output-filter "Data[].{id: id, name: name, email: profile.email}"
139-```
140-
141-Common JMESPath patterns:
142-
143-| Pattern | Effect |
144-|---|---|
145-| `Data[]` | Return all records (unwrap the Data envelope) |
146-| `Data[].name` | Return just the `name` field from each record |
147-| `Data[].{id: id, name: name}` | Return selected fields as objects |
148-| `Data[?status=='active']` | Filter records by field value |
149-| `Data[0]` | Return only the first record |
150-
151----
152-
153-## Pagination
154-
155-`uip is resources run list` may not return all results in a single call. **Always check for pagination** when searching for a specific item or listing all items.
156-
157-### Pagination rules
158-
159-1. **Always check `Data.Pagination`** — every `list` response may contain pagination state. Never assume a single page contains all results.
160-2. **Complete the pagination loop** — when searching for a specific item, keep paginating until `Data.Pagination.HasMore` is `"false"` or the item is found. Do NOT abandon pagination mid-loop to try alternative APIs (e.g., search endpoints, admin endpoints, HTTP fallback).
161-3. **Stop early on match** — if you find the target item in the current page, stop. No need to fetch remaining pages.

commands.result_summary: /home/azureuser/projects/skills/skills/uipath-agents/references/lowcode/model-selection-guide.md

1	# Model Selection Guide
2	
3	How to pick the LLM for a low-code agent's `settings.model`. The tenant is the source of truth — discover at runtime, then select; never ship the scaffold default.
4	
5	> `uip agent init` for an autonomous agent scaffolds `settings.model: "gpt-5.4"` with a 128000 output cap. **Always override it** with a discovered current model before validating.
6	
7	> `uip agent init --conversational` for a conversational agent scaffolds `settings.model: "anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0"` with a 64000 output cap. It serves as a solid default but can be overwritten with a discovered current model before validating. 
8	
9	## 1. Discover (primary path)
10	
11	List the models the authenticated tenant actually offers:
12	
13	```bash
14	uip agent model list --output json
15	```
16	
17	`Data` is a **flat array of PascalCase objects** — not nested, not lowercase:
18	
19	| Field | Meaning |
20	|-------|---------|
21	| `Provider` | `OpenAi` \| `AwsBedrock` \| `VertexAi` |
22	| `Name` | The exact string for `settings.model` (e.g. `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, `gpt-5.4`) |
23	| `IsByo` | `true` = bring-your-own key registered for this tenant |
24	| `IsPreview` | `true` = preview/non-GA — avoid by default |
25	| `MaxTokens` | Output-token ceiling for this model — caps `settings.maxTokens` |
26	
27	Filter to selectable GA models with `--output-filter` (a global flag applied to `Data` — write the JMESPath starting at `Data`, no `Data.` prefix):
28	
29	```bash
30	uip agent model list --output json \
31	  --output-filter "[?IsByo==\`false\` && IsPreview==\`false\`].{Name:Name,Provider:Provider,MaxTokens:MaxTokens}"
32	```
33	
34	Run discovery **before** choosing a model. Do not pick from this doc's examples without confirming the name appears in the live list — model availability differs per tenant and changes over time.
35	
36	## 2. Select
37	
38	1. Start from the GA-filtered list above (`IsByo=false`, `IsPreview=false`).
39	2. **Preview models are opt-in only.** Use an `IsPreview: true` model (e.g. `gpt-5.5-2026-04-23`, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`) **only when the user explicitly asks** for the bleeding edge — preview models can change behavior or availability without notice.
40	3. Pick the **newest GA model matching the task class** (§3).
41	4. Set `settings.maxTokens` from the chosen model's `MaxTokens` — never exceed the cap. Example: `gpt-4o-2024-11-20` caps at 16384, so `maxTokens: 32768` is invalid for it; `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` caps at 64000; `gpt-5.4` at 128000.
42	
43	## 3. Task → model mapping
44	
45	Express the choice as **selection criteria over the discovered list**, not a fixed ID:
46	
47	| Task class | Selection criterion | Why |
48	|------------|---------------------|-----|
49	| Reasoning / judgment / multi-step tool use | Newest GA Anthropic Sonnet or Opus, or newest GA flagship OpenAI | Strongest instruction-following + tool-call discipline |
50	| Fast / cheap / high-volume classification or extraction | Newest GA `*-mini` (e.g. an OpenAI `*-mini`) or GA Haiku | Lower latency + cost; sufficient for narrow deterministic tasks |
51	| Long-context (large documents, big tool outputs) | GA model with the highest `MaxTokens` | Avoids truncated output |
52	| Conversational | Newest GA Anthropic Sonnet or user preference | Strongest conversational responses and instruction-following |
53	
54	Concrete GA examples observed on a live tenant — **illustrative only; verify against `uip agent model list`**:
55	
56	- Reasoning: `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, `anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14`
57	- Fast/cheap: `gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17`, `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14`, `anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`
58	
59	## 4. Fallback (discovery unavailable)
60	
61	If `uip agent model list` fails (not logged in, offline, command unavailable), pick a curated GA default — currently `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` for reasoning tasks — and **tell the user it was not tenant-verified** and may not exist on their tenant. This is the only situation where a hardcoded name is the operative choice; everywhere else, discover first.
62	
63	## 5. Apply the choice
64	
65	Edit `settings.model` (and `settings.maxTokens`) in `agent.json`, then refresh and validate:
66	
67	1. Set `settings.model` to the discovered `Name`.
68	2. Set `settings.maxTokens` ≤ the model's `MaxTokens`.
69	3. `uip agent refresh --output json`
70	4. `uip agent validate --output json`
71	
72	For inline-in-flow agents add `--inline-in-flow` to both commands. Full field reference: [agent-definition.md](agent-definition.md#change-model-settings).
73

commands.result_summary:
1	# Autonomous Agents Prompting Guide
2	
3	This is the prompting guide for low-code autonomous agents.
4	
5	"Coding-agent-centric" = the prompt makes the embedded agent behave like a disciplined tool-using agent: explicit tool-call criteria, stop conditions, structured output. Maps to the agent's `tool` artifact ports and `outputSchema`.
6	
7	## 1. System-prompt skeleton
8	
9	Copy this skeleton, fill every slot. Consistent structure → consistent runs. Put role/behavior here; data/task goes in the user message (§2).
10	
11	```text
12	You are <ROLE> for <DOMAIN>. <ONE-LINE PURPOSE>.
13	
14	Scope:
15	- In scope: <what the agent handles>
16	- Out of scope: <what to refuse or escalate>
17	
18	Tools:
19	- <toolName>: call when <explicit condition>. Do not call when <condition>. Call at most <N> times (N ≤ 3 for a single decision).
20	- <toolName>: ...
21	Stop calling tools once <stop condition>; then produce the final answer.
22	If a tool result does not cover a detail, say so in <rationaleField>, lower <confidenceField>, and still return every outputSchema field. Never end a run without a final answer.
23	
24	Output:
25	- Return a result conforming to the output schema. <field>: <how to fill it>.
26	- Never invent fields or values not grounded in the input or a tool result.
27	
28	Uncertainty:
29	- If <required input> is missing or ambiguous, <ask | set field to null | escalate> — do not guess.
30	- If you cannot complete the task, return <explicit failure shape>, not a fabricated answer.
31	```
32	
33	Slot rules:
34	
35	- **Role + scope** — name the role, bound it. An unbounded agent answers off-task prompts.
36	- **Tool-call criteria** — one trigger condition per tool, plus a stop condition. Without this the agent over-calls or loops to `maxIterations`.
37	- **Output contract** — state that output MUST match `outputSchema`; map each field. Without it the agent free-forms prose.
38	- **Grounding** — forbid values not traceable to input or tool output. Cuts hallucination.
39	- **Iteration budget** — for multi-tool tasks, note the agent has limited iterations (`maxIterations`, default 25) and should act, not deliberate.
40	
41	## 2. User-prompt anatomy
42	
43	The user message carries the task and the data — not the role.
44	
45	```text
46	<TASK INSTRUCTION>.
47	
48	<LABEL>: {{ $vars.<flowNodeId>.output.<field> }}
49	<LABEL>: {{ $vars.<flowNodeId>.output.<field> }}
50	
51	<EXPLICIT OUTPUT INSTRUCTION — e.g. "Return the category and a one-sentence reason.">
52	```
53	
54	Token form depends on context:
55	
56	- **Inline-in-flow agents** reference upstream flow nodes: `{{ $vars.<flowNodeId>.output[.<field>] }}`. See the [uipath-maestro-flow inline-agent prompt-wiring guide](../../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/author/references/plugins/inline-agent/impl.md#wiring-flow-variables-into-agent-prompts).
57	- **Standalone agents** reference declared inputs: `{{input.<field>}}`.
58	
59	Mirror every `{{ ... }}` in `contentTokens[]` per [agent-definition.md § contentTokens Construction](../agent-definition.md#contenttokens-construction).
60	
61	## 3. Grounding in wired data
62	
63	Reference inputs through tokens — never restate their literal contents in prose. The runtime injects the value; restating it duplicates tokens and risks drift if the upstream field changes. Tell the agent *what the field is*, not *what it contains*.
64	
65	## 4. Worked example — email triage
66	
67	Realistic inline-in-flow agent. Note the **structured `outputSchema`**, not a bare `content` blob.
68	
69	**Before (toy):**
70	
71	```json
72	"settings": { "model": "gpt-5.4" },
73	"outputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "content": { "type": "string" } } },
74	"messages": [
75	  { "role": "system", "content": "You are an assistant." },
76	  { "role": "user", "content": "Triage this email." }
77	]
78	```
79	
80	**After (robust):**
81	
82	```json
83	"settings": { "model": "anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6", "temperature": 0, "maxTokens": 4096, "maxIterations": 10 },
84	"outputSchema": {
85	  "type": "object",
86	  "properties": {
87	    "category": { "type": "string", "description": "One of: billing, technical, sales, other" },
88	    "priority": { "type": "string", "description": "low | medium | high | urgent" },
89	    "reason":   { "type": "string", "description": "One sentence justifying the category" },
90	    "needsHuman": { "type": "boolean", "description": "true if the email requires human review" }
91	  },
92	  "required": ["category", "priority", "needsHuman"]
93	}
94	```
95	
96	System prompt (filled skeleton):
97	
98	```text
99	You are a support-email triage classifier for a SaaS product. Classify each inbound email and flag those needing a human.
100	
101	Scope:
102	- In scope: categorizing the email and assessing priority.
103	- Out of scope: replying to the customer or taking any action — only classify.
104	
105	Output:
106	- Return a result conforming to the output schema. category MUST be one of billing, technical, sales, other. priority MUST be low, medium, high, or urgent.
107	- Set needsHuman=true for legal threats, churn risk, or anything outside the four categories.
108	- Never invent customer details not present in the email.
109	
110	Uncertainty:
111	- If the email is empty or unintelligible, set category="other", needsHuman=true, reason="unintelligible input".
112	```
113	
114	User prompt:
115	
116	```text
117	Classify the following email.
118	
119	From: {{ $vars.emailReceived1.output.from }}
120	Subject: {{ $vars.emailReceived1.output.subject }}
121	
122	{{ $vars.emailReceived1.output.body }}
123	
124	Return category, priority, a one-sentence reason, and needsHuman.
125	```
126	
127	## 5. Production checklist — adjacent `agent.json` quality fields
128	
129	A robust agent is more than its prompt. Each field: default, and when to change.
130	
131	| Field | Default | Change when |
132	|-------|---------|-------------|
133	| `outputSchema` | Scaffold gives a single `content` string | **Almost always** — define typed fields a downstream node can consume. Bare `content` forces brittle string-parsing. |
134	| `settings.temperature` | `0` | Keep `0` for extraction/classification/judgment. Raise only when output *variation* is wanted (drafting, brainstorming). |
135	| `settings.maxIterations` | `25` | `≤5` only if tool-less and single-shot. Kill switch, not a loop fix: without a per-tool cap the agent loops to the ceiling — observed dying at 5 and at 25 alike (`TERMINATION_MAX_ITERATIONS`). |
136	| `settings.maxTokens` | Scaffold value | Set ≤ the model's `MaxTokens` cap — see [model-selection-guide.md](../model-selection-guide.md#1-discover-primary-path). |
137	| `settings.model` | `gpt-5.4` | **Always override** — discover + select per [model-selection-guide.md](../model-selection-guide.md). |
138	| `guardrails` | `[]` | Add input/output policy enforcement (PII, content, escalation). See [capabilities/guardrails/guardrails.md](../capabilities/guardrails/guardrails.md). |
139	
140	## Anti-patterns
141	
142	- **Vague role** — "You are a helpful agentic assistant." Name the role and bound the scope.
143	- **No output contract** — agent free-forms prose; downstream nodes can't parse it.
144	- **Bare `content` output** — a single string where typed fields belong. Define `outputSchema`.
145	- **No tool-call criteria** — agent over-calls tools or loops to `maxIterations`.
146	- **Prompt-injection-prone passthrough** — pasting untrusted input into the system prompt. Keep untrusted data in the user message; keep instructions in the system message.
147	- **Ignoring `outputSchema`** — prompt that doesn't tell the agent to conform to the declared schema.
148	- **Cargo-culted `temperature`** — copying a nonzero temperature into a deterministic classification task.
149

commands.result_summary: /home/azureuser/projects/skills/skills/uipath-agents/references/lowcode/capabilities/context/index.md

1	# Index Context (Context Grounding RAG)
2	
3	Walkthrough for adding a context resource backed by an ECS Context Grounding index. Used for RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) — the agent issues queries against the index and gets back relevant chunks.
4	
5	For other context variants, see [context.md](context.md).
6	
7	## When to Use
8	
9	- Agent needs to retrieve from a knowledge base of indexed documents
10	- The index already exists in Context Grounding and is backed by an Orchestrator storage bucket. To create or manage that index from the CLI, see [uipath-platform/references/context-grounding/index-management.md](../../../../../uipath-platform/references/context-grounding/index-management.md)
11	
12	`uip solution resources refresh` emits an `index` binding into `bindings_v2.json`, resolves the backing storage bucket via ECS + Orchestrator, and writes all three artifacts automatically: `resources/solution_folder/index/<IndexName>.json`, `resources/solution_folder/bucket/orchestratorBucket/<BucketName>.json`, and two `debug_overwrites.json` entries (`kind: "index"`, `kind: "bucket"`). No manual solution-level authoring is required.
13	
14	**Only `contextType: "index"` with a StorageBucket data source is supported.** `attachments` and `datafabricentityset` contexts, and indexes backed by GoogleDrive / OneDrive / Dropbox / Confluence, emit a warning from refresh and must be hand-authored.
15	
16	## Discovery
17	
18	Two `uip` calls — identity from `resource list`, full configuration from `resource get`. Symmetric with [../process/process.md § Discovery](../process/process.md#discovery).
19	
20	### Step 1 — Verify login and scaffold (if not already done)
21	
22	Run `uip login status --output json`. If a solution and agent do not yet exist, scaffold per [../../project-lifecycle.md § End-to-End Example](../../project-lifecycle.md#end-to-end-example--new-standalone-agent).
23	
24	### Step 2 — Find the index (identity)
25	
26	```bash
27	uip solution resources list --kind Index --source remote --search "<INDEX_NAME>" --output json
28	```
29	
30	Response wrapper: `{Result, Code: "ResourceList", Data: [...]}` — parse `.Data[]`.
31	
32	| Field | Use as |
33	|-------|--------|
34	| `Key` | index GUID — pass to `resource get` in Step 3. Not stored in the agent resource. |
35	| `Name` | exact `indexName` to set in the context resource → also propagates as binding `name` |
36	| `Folder` | literal folder path → top-level `folderPath` (e.g., `"Shared/Knowledge"`) and binding `folderPath`. Refresh uses `(name, folderPath)` jointly to look up the index in ECS. |
37	| `FolderKey` | folder GUID. Refresh resolves it from `Folder`; informational here. |
38	
39	When the same `Name` repeats across folders, pick by `Key`.
40	
41	### Step 3 — Get the index configuration
42	
43	```bash
44	uip solution resources get <KEY> --output json
45	```
46	
47	Response wrapper: `{Result, Code: "ResourceConfiguration", Data: {...}}`. `Data.spec` is the source-of-truth that `uip solution resources refresh` round-trips into `resources/solution_folder/index/<IndexName>.json` — confirm it before authoring.
48	
49	| `Data.spec` field | Confirms / Use as |
50	|-------|------------------|
51	| `dataSourceType` | MUST equal `"StorageBucket"`. Anything else (GoogleDrive / OneDrive / Dropbox / Confluence / Attachments) — refresh warns + skips. Hand-author solution-level files or escalate. |
52	| `storageBucketReference.name` | Bucket display name. Refresh writes this as the bucket manifest's `name`. Optionally cross-check with `uip solution resources list --kind Bucket --source remote --search "<NAME>" --output json` to confirm the bucket is reachable. |
53	| `storageBucketReference.key` | Bucket GUID — refresh writes this verbatim as `key` in the bucket manifest and as `dependencies[].key` / `spec.storageBucketReference.key` in the index manifest. |
54	| `storageBucketReference.folderKey` | Folder GUID containing the bucket. Matches the index's `FolderKey` from Step 2 (the bucket lives in the same folder as the index). |
55	| `fileNameGlob` | File-extension filter on the index itself. Sanity-check — does not need to match the agent resource's `settings.fileExtension.value`. |
56	| `includeSubfolders`, `ingestionType`, `encrypted` | Reference fields — refresh round-trips them into the solution-level index manifest. |
57	
58	Wrapper-level `apiVersion` is `"ecs.uipath.com/v2"` — matches what refresh writes.
59	
60	## Agent-Level Resource Shape
61	
62	**Path:** `<AgentName>/resources/<ContextName>/resource.json`
63	
64	```jsonc
65	{
66	  "$resourceType": "context",
67	  "id": "<uuid>",                       // stable; generate once
68	  "referenceKey": null,                 // leave null; refresh resolves the ECS index GUID by indexName
69	  "name": "<ContextName>",              // display name; matches the folder under resources/
70	  "description": "",
71	  "contextType": "index",
72	  "folderPath": "Shared/Knowledge",     // Literal Folder from `uip solution resources list`. Propagates verbatim into bindings_v2.json.
73	  "indexName": "<IndexName>",           // MUST match the ECS index Name exactly (case-sensitive)
74	  "settings": {
75	    "retrievalMode": "semantic",        // "semantic" | "structured" | "deeprag" | "batchtransform"
76	    "query": { "variant": "dynamic", "description": "Query for retrieval" },
77	    "folderPathPrefix": { "variant": "static" },
78	    "fileExtension": { "value": "All" },  // object, not string
79	    "threshold": 0,
80	    "resultCount": 3
81	  }
82	}
83	```
84	
85	**`retrievalMode` values (all lowercase) and per-mode `fileExtension.value` + extra fields:**
86	
87	| `retrievalMode` | Legal `fileExtension.value` | Extra required fields |
88	|---|---|---|
89	| `"semantic"` | `"All"`, `"pdf"`, `"csv"`, `"json"`, `"docx"`, `"xlsx"`, `"txt"` | none |
90	| `"structured"` | `"csv"` | none |
91	| `"deeprag"` | `"pdf"`, `"txt"` | `"citationMode": { "value": "Inline" }` (or `"Skip"`) |
92	| `"batchtransform"` | `"csv"` | `"webSearchGrounding": { "value": "Enabled" }` (or `"Disabled"`), `"outputColumns": [{ "name": "...", "description": "..." }, ...]` |
93	
94	**`query.variant`:** `"dynamic"` (LLM supplies at runtime), `"argument"` (bound to an input field), or `"static"` (pre-set value).
95	
96	**`folderPathPrefix.variant`:** `"static"` (no prefix) or `"argument"` (scope by a folder path provided at runtime).
97	
98	**Casing matters.** All `contextType` and `retrievalMode` values are lowercase. See [../../critical-rules/critical-rules.md](../../critical-rules/critical-rules.md) Anti-pattern 12.
99	
100	## Solution-Level Files
101	
102	For `contextType: "index"` with a StorageBucket-backed ECS index, `uip agent refresh` emits:
103	
104	```json
105	{
106	  "resource": "index",
107	  "key": "<IndexName>",
108	  "value": {
109	    "name":       { "defaultValue": "<IndexName>", "isExpression": false, "displayName": "Index Name" },
110	    "folderPath": { "defaultValue": "<Folder>",    "isExpression": false }
111	  },
112	  "metadata": { "bindingsVersion": "2.2", "solutionsSupport": "true" }
113	}
114	```
115	
116	into `bindings_v2.json` at the agent project root. `folderPath` is propagated verbatim from the agent-level `resource.json`'s top-level `folderPath` field. `uip solution resources refresh` then:
117	
118	1. Calls ECS `GET ecs_/v2/indexes/AllAcrossFolders?$filter=Name eq '<IndexName>'&$expand=dataSource` — resolves the index GUID, folder key, and data source type. With the binding's `folderPath` set, refresh narrows multi-folder name collisions to the exact deployment.
119	2. If `dataSource.@odata.type` is not `#UiPath.Vdbs.Domain.Api.V20Models.StorageBucketDataSource`, warns + skips (other data sources — GoogleDrive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Confluence, Attachments — are not yet wired).
120	3. Calls Orchestrator `GET orchestrator_/odata/Buckets?$filter=Name eq '<BucketName>'` with the index's `folderKey` as `X-UIPATH-FolderKey` — gets the bucket `Identifier` GUID.
121	4. Registers the bucket as a solution resource via the resource-builder SDK — writes `resources/solution_folder/bucket/orchestratorBucket/<BucketName>.json`.
122	5. Hand-writes `resources/solution_folder/index/<IndexName>.json` with `kind: "index"`, `apiVersion: "ecs.uipath.com/v2"`, `dependencies: [{name: "<BucketName>", kind: "bucket"}]`, `spec.storageBucketReference: { name, key }`, `dataSourceType: "StorageBucket"`.
123	6. Appends two entries (`kind: "index"` + `kind: "bucket"`) to `userProfile/<userId>/debug_overwrites.json`.
124	
125	All failures (index not found, ambiguous name match, non-StorageBucket data source, bucket missing in Orchestrator) warn + continue — the command never aborts.
126	
127	### Index Definition (refresh fallback)
128	
129	**Path:** `resources/solution_folder/index/{IndexName}.json`
130	
131	```jsonc
132	{
133	  "docVersion": "1.0.0",
134	  "resource": {
135	    "name": "MyIndex",
136	    "kind": "index",
137	    "apiVersion": "ecs.uipath.com/v2",
138	    "isOverridable": true,
139	    "dependencies": [
140	      {
141	        "name": "my_storage_bucket",
142	        "kind": "bucket",
143	        "key": "<bucket-resource-uuid>"
144	      }
145	    ],
146	    "spec": {
147	      "name": "MyIndex",
148	      "description": "",
149	      "storageBucketReference": {
150	        "name": "my_storage_bucket",
151	        "key": "<bucket-resource-uuid>"
152	      },
153	      "fileNameGlob": "All",
154	      "dataSourceType": "StorageBucket",
155	      "includeSubfolders": true,
156	      "ingestionType": "Advanced"
157	    },
158	    "key": "<unique-uuid>"
159	  }
160	}
161	```
162	
163	### Storage Bucket Definition (refresh fallback)
164	
165	**Path:** `resources/solution_folder/bucket/orchestratorBucket/{BucketName}.json`
166	
167	```jsonc
168	{
169	  "docVersion": "1.0.0",
170	  "resource": {
171	    "name": "my_storage_bucket",
172	    "kind": "bucket",
173	    "type": "orchestratorBucket",
174	    "apiVersion": "orchestrator.uipath.com/v1",
175	    "isOverridable": true,
176	    "spec": {
177	      "type": "Orchestrator",
178	      "description": null,
179	      "tags": []
180	    },
181	    "key": "<unique-uuid>"
182	  }
183	}
184	```
185	
186	## Walkthrough
187	
188	### Step 4 — Create the agent-level context resource
189	
190	**Path:** `<AgentName>/resources/<ContextName>/resource.json`
191	
192	```jsonc
193	{
194	  "$resourceType": "context",
195	  "id": "<uuid>",                       // generate a fresh UUID
196	  "referenceKey": null,
197	  "name": "<ContextName>",
198	  "description": "",
199	  "contextType": "index",
200	  "folderPath": "<FOLDER>",             // literal Folder from Step 2 (e.g., "Shared/Knowledge")
201	  "indexName": "<INDEX_NAME>",          // exact ECS index name from Step 2
202	  "settings": {
203	    "retrievalMode": "semantic",
204	    "query": { "variant": "dynamic" },
205	    "folderPathPrefix": { "variant": "static" },
206	    "fileExtension": { "value": "All" },
207	    "threshold": 0,
208	    "resultCount": 3
209	  }
210	}
211	```
212	
213	See § Agent-Level Resource Shape above for the full field reference, including the three variants (`index`/`attachments`/`datafabricentityset`) and per-`retrievalMode` settings (`citationMode` for `deeprag`, `webSearchGrounding` + `outputColumns` for `batchtransform`).
214	
215	### Step 4b — Inline agents only: wire the context flow node
216	
217	**Skip if the agent is standalone.** If the context is on an **inline** agent (embedded in a flow), the `resource.json` alone is never reached at runtime — you MUST also add a `uipath.agent.resource.context.index.<index-name>.<index-id>` flow node connected to the autonomous node's `context` handle (bottom port). Fetch its manifest with `uip maestro flow registry get "<NodeType>" --output json`, then hand the node + edge authoring to the `uipath-maestro-flow` skill (Critical Rule 16 — this skill does not author `.flow` graphs directly). Run Step 5's refresh/validate with `--inline-in-flow` plus `--bindings-target <FlowProjectDir>/bindings_v2.json`. See [../inline-in-flow/inline-in-flow.md](../inline-in-flow/inline-in-flow.md).
218	
219	### Step 5 — Refresh and validate
220	
221	```bash
222	uip agent refresh  "<AGENT_NAME>" --output json
223	uip agent validate "<AGENT_NAME>" --output json
224	```
225	
226	Refresh writes the binding. Validate is read-only. Confirm `Validated.resources` includes the context, then inspect the emitted binding:
227	
228	```bash
229	cat "<AGENT_NAME>/bindings_v2.json"
230	# Expect: resources[0] with {resource: "index", key: "<INDEX_NAME>", ...}
231	```
232	
233	### Step 6 — Refresh solution resources
234	
235	```bash
236	uip solution resources refresh --output json
237	```
238	
239	Refresh resolves the index via ECS `$expand=dataSource`, locates its backing StorageBucket in Orchestrator, and writes:
240	
241	- `resources/solution_folder/index/<INDEX_NAME>.json` — manifest with `kind: "index"`, `apiVersion: "ecs.uipath.com/v2"`, `dependencies: [{name, kind: "bucket"}]`, `spec.storageBucketReference.{name,key}`.
242	- `resources/solution_folder/bucket/orchestratorBucket/<BucketName>.json` — standard bucket manifest.
243	- `userProfile/<userId>/debug_overwrites.json` — two entries (`kind: "index"` and `kind: "bucket"`), both referencing the index's folder.
244	
245	Check the `Warnings` array in the refresh output. Common warnings:
246	- `Index "<NAME>" not found in ECS` — exact-name mismatch. Re-check the index name.
247	- `Index uses <type>, which is not yet supported` — data source is GoogleDrive/OneDrive/Dropbox/Confluence/Attachments; hand-author the solution-level files. Step 3's `dataSourceType` check should have caught this earlier.
248	- `Storage bucket "<NAME>" not found in Orchestrator folder` — the bucket was deleted or lives in a different folder than the index.
249	
250	### Step 7 — Bundle and upload
251	
252	```bash
253	uip solution bundle . -d ./dist --output json
254	uip solution upload ./dist/<SOLUTION_NAME>.uis --output json
255	```
256	
257	The upload response includes a `Data.DesignerUrl` — open it to verify the context appears wired to the ECS index in Studio Web.
258	
259	## Gotchas
260	
261	`contextType` and `retrievalMode` values MUST be lowercase — see [../../critical-rules/critical-rules.md](../../critical-rules/critical-rules.md) Anti-pattern 12.
262	
263	**Cap retrievals in the system prompt.** Wiring the index is not enough: "ground your answer in the retrieved guidance" with no call limit makes the agent re-query with new phrasings until the runtime terminates it — `AGENT_RUNTIME.TERMINATION_MAX_ITERATIONS` (in a flow: node Failed, incident `170002`). Raising `settings.maxIterations` only moves the failure — 5 dies at 5, 25 dies at 25. State a cap and a fallback:
264	
265	```text
266	Call <toolName> at most <N> times (N ≤ 3 for a single decision). After the last call, stop retrieving and decide with the evidence you already have.
267	If the retrieved content does not cover a detail, say so in <rationaleField>, lower <confidenceField>, and still return every outputSchema field. Never end a run without a determination.
268	```
269	
270	## References
271	
272	- [context.md](context.md) — capability overview and variant decision
273	- [attachments.md](attachments.md) — runtime file attachments
274	- [datafabric.md](datafabric.md) — DataFabric entity-set context
275	- [../../solution-resources.md](../../solution-resources.md) § Refresh Mechanics
